author: yonesnou
quote:
What makes GTA VI so disappointing is that, despite its impressive graphics and technical advancements, it seems to have lost much of the personality that made the franchise great in the first place.

The biggest issue is the story, particularly its main characters. The narrative feels boring, and the protagonists lack the charisma, depth, and eccentric personalities that made characters like Trevor, Michael, and CJ so memorable. Their relationship fails to remain engaging, and the overall story feels more like a conventional crime drama than an authentic Grand Theft Auto experience.

Another major disappointment is the lack of the dark, irreverent, and politically incorrect humor that has always been one of Rockstar's trademarks. Previous GTA games made fun of absolutely everything: society, politics, the media, consumerism, and American culture itself. They weren't afraid to be provocative, absurd, offensive, or downright outrageous. That satirical edge seems to have been toned down, taking away a fundamental part of what made the franchise unique.

On top of that, several gameplay decisions unnecessarily restrict the player's freedom. Invulnerable NPCs completely undermine the sense of freedom that has always defined GTA. The removal of mission replayability is another frustrating step backward, especially for players who enjoyed experimenting with different approaches or simply revisiting their favorite missions.

And then there are the household chores, cleaning, grocery shopping, and other mundane activities. There's a difference between adding optional activities that make an open world feel alive and turning everyday errands into actual gameplay content. Realism doesn't automatically make something fun, and doing virtual household chores is hardly what most people expect from a Grand Theft Auto game.

Ultimately, GTA VI might be a technical masterpiece, but technical achievements alone don't make a great GTA game. The franchise was built around freedom, chaos, satire, memorable characters, and the ability to do things that would be completely unacceptable in real life. When those elements are compromised in favor of realism and routine activities, it's fair to question whether Rockstar has lost sight of what made GTA special in the first place.

A bigger, prettier world doesn't necessarily make a better Grand Theft Auto
